segments.arabic:
تقدم نسبها في ترجمة أخيها حرام بن ملحان، وهي أم أنس خادم رسول اللَّه ﵌، اشتهرت بكنيتها.
واختلف في اسمها، فقيل سهلة، وقيل رميلة، وقيل رميثة، وقيل مليكة، وقيل الغميصاء أو الرّميصاء تزوّجت مالك بن النضر في الجاهليّة، فولدت أنسا في الجاهليّة، وأسلمت مع السّابقين إلى الإسلام من الأنصار، فغضب مالك وخرج إلى الشّام فمات بها، فتزوّجت بعده أبا طلحة، فروينا في مسند أحمد بعلوّ في الغيلانيات، من طريق حمّاد بن سلمة، عن ثابت، وإسماعيل بن عبد الله بن أبي طلحة، عن أنس بن مالك- أن أبا طلحة خطب أم سليم- يعني قبل أن يسلم، فقالت: يا أبا طلحة، ألست تعلم أن إلهك الّذي تعبد نبت من الأرض؟ قال: بلى. قلت: أفلا تستحي تعبد شجرة! إن أسلمت فإنّي لا أريد منك صداقا غيره.
قال: حتى انظر في أمري، فذهب ثم جاء، فقال: أشهد أن لا إله إلا اللَّه وأنّ محمدا رسول اللَّه، فقالت: يا أنس، زوّج أبا طلحة، فزوّجها.
ولهذا الحديث طرق متعددة. وقال ابن سعد: أخبرنا خالد بن مخلد، حدّثني محمد بن موسى، عن عبد اللَّه بن عبد اللَّه بن أبي طلحة، عن أنس بن مالك، قال: خطب أبو طلحة أم سليم، فقالت: إني قد آمنت بهذا الرّجل، وشهدت بأنه رسول اللَّه، فإن تابعتني تزوّجتك. قال: فأنا على ما أنت عليه، فتزوّجته أم سليم، وكان صداقها الإسلام.
وبه: خطب أبو طلحة أم سليم- وكانت أم سليم تقول: لا أتزوج حتى يبلغ أنس ويجلس في المجالس، فيقول: جزى اللَّه أمي عنّي خيرا، لقد أحسنت ولايتي. فقال لها أبو طلحة: فقد جلس أنس وتكلم، فتزوّجها.
أخبرنا مسلم بن إبراهيم، أخبرنا ربعي بن عبد اللَّه بن الجارود، حدّثني أنس بن مالك- أن النبيّ ﵌ كان يزور أمّ سليم فتتحفه بالشّيء تصنعه له «١» .
أخبرنا عمرو بن عاصم، حدّثنا همام، حدّثنا إسحاق، عن أنس، أنه حدّثهم: لم يكن رسول اللَّه ﵌ يدخل بيتا غير بيت أم سليم إلا على أزواجه، فقيل له. فقال: إني أرحمها، قتل أخوها وأبوها معي.
قلت: والجواب عن دخوله بيت أم حرام وأختها أنهما كانتا في دار واحدة، وكانت
(١) أخرجه ابن سعد في الطبقات الكبرى ٨/ ٣١٣ بلفظه.
segments.english:
Her lineage was given above in the biography of her brother Haram ibn Milhan. She was the mother of Anas, the servant of the Messenger of Allah—may Allah bless him and grant him peace—and she became well known by her kunyah.

There is disagreement concerning her name. It is said to have been Sahla, Rumayla, Rumaytha, Mulayka, al-Ghumaysa, or al-Rumaysa. She married Malik ibn al-Nadr during the pre-Islamic period and bore Anas during that period. She embraced Islam together with the earliest of the Ansar to accept Islam. Malik became angry, departed for Syria, and died there. After him, she married Abu Talha.

We transmitted in Musnad Ahmad, through an elevated chain in al-Ghaylaniyyat, by way of Hammad ibn Salama, from Thabit and Isma'il ibn Abd Allah ibn Abu Talha, from Anas ibn Malik, that Abu Talha proposed marriage to Umm Sulaym—that is, before he embraced Islam. She said, “Abu Talha, do you not know that the god you worship grew from the earth?” He replied, “Yes.” She said, “Are you not ashamed to worship a tree? If you embrace Islam, I desire no bridal gift from you other than that.”

He said, “Let me consider my situation.” He departed and then returned, saying, “I bear witness that there is no deity but Allah and that Muhammad is the Messenger of Allah.” She said, “Anas, marry me to Abu Talha,” and Anas gave her in marriage to him.

This hadith has several chains of transmission. Ibn Sa'd said: Khalid ibn Makhlad informed us: Muhammad ibn Musa related to me, from Abd Allah ibn Abd Allah ibn Abu Talha, from Anas ibn Malik, who said: Abu Talha proposed marriage to Umm Sulaym. She said, “I have believed in this man and borne witness that he is the Messenger of Allah. If you follow me, I will marry you.” He said, “Then I am upon the same faith as you.” Umm Sulaym therefore married him, and Islam was her bridal gift.

By the same chain: Abu Talha proposed marriage to Umm Sulaym. Umm Sulaym used to say, “I will not marry until Anas comes of age and sits in the assemblies, saying, ‘May Allah reward my mother well on my behalf; she cared for me excellently.’” Abu Talha said to her, “Anas has now sat in the assemblies and spoken,” so he married her.

Muslim ibn Ibrahim informed us: Rib'i ibn Abd Allah ibn al-Jarud informed us: Anas ibn Malik related to me that the Prophet—may Allah bless him and grant him peace—used to visit Umm Sulaym, and she would present him with something she had prepared for him.¹

Amr ibn Asim informed us: Hammam related to us: Ishaq related to us, from Anas, that he told them: The Messenger of Allah—may Allah bless him and grant him peace—would not enter any house other than the house of Umm Sulaym, except when visiting his wives. He was asked about this, and he replied, “I have compassion for her; her brother and her father were killed alongside me.”

segments.arabic:
تغزو مع رسول اللَّه ﵌، ولها قصص مشهورة، منها ما أخرجه ابن سعد بسند صحيح أن أم سليم اتخذت خنجرا يوم حنين، فقال أبو طلحة: يا رسول اللَّه، هذه أم سليم معها خنجر، فقالت: اتخذته إن دنا مني أحد من المشركين بقرت بطنه.
ومنها قصّتها المخرجة في الصّحيح لما مات ولدها ابن أبي طلحة، فقالت لما دخل:
لا يذكر أحد ذلك لأبي طلحة قبلي، فلما جاء وسأل عن ولده قالت: هو أسكن ما كان، فظنّ أنه عوفي، وقام فأكل ثم تزيّنت له وتطيّبت فنام معها، وأصاب منها، فلما أصبح قالت له: احتسب ولدك، فذكر ذلك للنبيّ ﵌ فقال: «بارك اللَّه لكما في ليلتكما»، فجاءت بولد وهو عبد اللَّه بن أبي طلحة، فأنجب ورزق أولادا، قرأ القرآن منهم عشرة كملا.
وقال الصّحيح أيضا عن أنس- أن أمّ سليم لما قدم النبيّ ﵌ قالت: يا رسول اللَّه، هذا أنس يخدمك، وكان حينئذ ابن عشر سنين، فخدم النّبيّ ﵌ منذ قدم المدينة حتى مات، فاشتهر بخادم النّبيّ ﵌.
وروت عن النّبيّ ﷺ عدة أحاديث، روى عنها ابنها أنس، وابن عباس، وزيد بن ثابت، وأبو سلمة بن عبد الرّحمن، وآخرون.
وذكر أبو عمر نسبها من كتاب ابن السّكن بحروفه، لكن قال: اسم أمها مليكة، والّذي في كتاب ابن السّكن اسم أمها أنيقة- نبّه عليه ابن فتحون، وكأن أبا عمر أخذه عن ابن سعد، فإنه جزم بأن أمها مليكة بنت مالك بن عديّ بن زيد مناة.
segments.english:
[She] used to go on military campaigns with the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace), and many well-known accounts are told of her. Among them is the report transmitted by Ibn Sa'd with a sound chain: on the day of Hunayn, Umm Sulaym took a dagger. Abu Talha said, “O Messenger of Allah, here is Umm Sulaym with a dagger.” She said, “I took it so that, if any of the polytheists comes near me, I will slit his belly open.”

Another is her story, transmitted in al-Sahih, concerning the death of her son by Abu Talha. When Abu Talha entered, she said, “Let no one mention this to Abu Talha before I do.” When he came and asked about his son, she said, “He is calmer than he has ever been.” He thought that the boy had recovered. He got up and ate; then she adorned and perfumed herself for him, and he slept with her and had intercourse with her. In the morning she said to him, “Seek Allah's reward for your son.” He mentioned this to the Prophet (may Allah bless him and grant him peace), who said, “May Allah bless you both in your night.” She then bore a son, namely Abd Allah ibn Abi Talha. He went on to sire distinguished offspring and was blessed with children, ten of whom recited the Qur'an in full.

al-Sahih also reports from Anas that, when the Prophet (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) arrived, Umm Sulaym said, “O Messenger of Allah, this is Anas; let him serve you.” He was ten years old at the time. He served the Prophet (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) from the Prophet's arrival in Medina until his death, and thus became famous as the servant of the Prophet (may Allah bless him and grant him peace).

She related a number of hadiths from the Prophet (may Allah bless him and grant him peace). Her son Anas, Ibn Abbas, Zayd ibn Thabit, Abu Salama ibn Abd al-Rahman, and others related from her.

Abu Umar reproduced her genealogy from the book of Ibn al-Sakan letter for letter, but said that her mother's name was Mulayka. What appears in Ibn al-Sakan's book, however, is that her mother's name was Aniqa. Ibn Fathun drew attention to this. It is as though Abu Umar took it from Ibn Sa'd, for he stated categorically that her mother was Mulayka bint Malik ibn Adi ibn Zayd Manat.
